entities.name: Ariarathes VI of Cappadocia
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Ariarathes VI Epiphanes Philopator, the youngest son of Ariarathes V of Cappadocia and Nysa of Cappadocia, was the Ariarathid king of Cappadocia from 130 BC to 116 BC.

As a member of the Hellenistic period's Hecatomnidae dynasty, Ariarathes VI sought to maintain Cappadocia's independence in the face of Roman expansion. The 30-year-old king successfully leveraged his strategic location to foster alliances with key Roman figures, including Julius Caesar and Pompey.

Despite his efforts, Ariarathes VI's reign was ultimately cut short when his successor, Ariarathes VII, seized the throne. This tumultuous period in Cappadocian history would have lasting implications for the region's politics and its place in the ancient world.

Ariarathes VI's legacy extends beyond his own reign, as he played a crucial role in shaping the Hecatomnidae dynasty's relationships with neighboring powers. His diplomatic maneuverings continue to fascinate historians seeking to understand the intricacies of ancient Cappadocian politics.

"We must always be wary of the ambitions of those who would seek to dominate the world," Ariarathes VI once said, his words a testament to the enduring significance of his rule.
